method: mechanical production-caller census plus six adversarially-verified source reads; every entry below is reproducible with rg over non-test Go

corrections.claim: in-flight coalescing is proved under 128-way concurrency with one payable and independent discounted receipts
corrections.accurate_part: POST /v1/chat/completions -> handleChatCompletions -> tryRealtimeCoalescedDelivery -> ClaimInflightExecution/AwaitInflightResult/ResolveInflightSuccess is a genuine production call graph, and the governed lease table inflight_executions exists
corrections.inaccurate_part: the 128-way test drives Store.ClaimInflightExecution directly, executes no work and settles no money; the money test is pure arithmetic against no database. The two halves are never joined, so no run has ever produced one physical execution and one supplier payable for 128 buyer deliveries

corrections.finding: RenewInflightLease has ZERO production callers. inflightLeaseTTL is 30 seconds, so any leader whose execution exceeds it can be taken over mid-flight in production.
sweepExpiredInflight has ZERO production callers and is not registered in the workers ticker table. Expired inflight_executions rows accumulate.

corrections.claim: coalesced deliveries are billed under their own class
corrections.finding: ClassCoalescedDelivery is declared and registered as non-physical but is never written. Followers settle through SettleRealtimeExactReuse and are recorded as exact_reuse, so coalesced revenue cannot be counted separately.
corrections.severity: reporting defect on a money row

corrections.claim: an operator or a test can force a governed job onto a named runtime cell
corrections.finding: buildWorkloadDecisionDirected has ZERO production callers. The mechanism is real and is reached only from tests; there is no operator entry point. Every llama.cpp chain proof therefore submits through a test-constructed job row rather than POST /v1/jobs.
corrections.corrected_classification: directed routing: IMPLEMENTED_UNWIRED for operators, exercised by tests

corrections.finding: the flag is inert. ClaimTaskSQL passes shapeNoPreference unconditionally and never calls preferenceForTier, which has zero production callers.
corrections.severity: an advertised switch that changes nothing

corrections.claim: value-ranked prefix cache eviction bounds worker_prefix_state
corrections.finding: EvictPrefixCacheToBudget and DeepestWarmPrefix have ZERO production callers. The scheduler uses its own inline warm-depth SQL, so two independent definitions exist and only one is live. worker_prefix_state is bounded only by a retention sweep.
SelectBatch and TokenBudgetFor have ZERO production callers, and one latency class (INTERACTIVE) is defined rather than the four the directive names.
